decisive_spans.text: High-resolution CT of the temporal bones showed an irregularly enhancing mass in the right ear canal, middle ear cavity, and mastoid air cells, with erosive changes of the skull base and extension into the right middle cranial fossa

response.rationale: D2 (Cholesteatoma) is strongly supported by the patient's symptoms of painless otorrhea, progressive hearing loss, and imaging findings of an irregularly enhancing mass in the ear canal, middle ear, and mastoid air cells. D4 (Squamous cell carcinoma of the external auditory canal) is also supported by the polypoid mass and purulent discharge, and erosive changes of the skull base. However, the involvement of the middle ear cavity and mastoid air cells, in addition to the external auditory canal, makes cholesteatoma a slightly better fit, as it can be extensive. The margin is low because both are strong contenders given the provided information.
